title: Axisymmetric transient heat
summary: Heat a finite cylinder from its rim and ends, inspect retained time frames and check the 190 s temperature against a published NAFEMS target and cylindrical diffusion.

steps.title: Start the cylinder section
steps.explain: Build the first, continuously heated scenario of the NAFEMS case used by COMSOL: a cylinder of radius 0.3 m and length 0.4 m, initially at 0 °C. Its curved wall and both ends jump to 1000 °C. We re-author the setup here; no vendor model or images are needed.

steps.title: Choose useful units
steps.explain: Use metres, seconds and degrees Celsius. Temperatures are absolute values; differences in kelvin and Celsius have the same numerical size.

steps.title: Revolve the physics, not the mesh
steps.explain: Choose axisymmetric: screen x is radius r and screen y is axial position z. A rectangular sheet represents the whole cylinder, with each quadrature point weighted by its circumference. It is not a flat plate.

steps.title: The meridian rectangle
steps.explain: The left edge r = 0 is the rotation axis. The lattice names its outside edges xmin, xmax, ymin and ymax; use xmax for the rim and ymin/ymax for the two ends. No artificial mechanical symmetry constraint belongs in this heat-only Step.

steps.title: Conductivity and heat storage
steps.explain: These are the published benchmark constants: conductivity 52 W/(m K), density 7850 kg/m³ and heat capacity 460 J/(kg K). No elastic modulus is needed for a heat-only Material.

doIt.name: thermal
doIt.source: NAFEMS thermal benchmark, COMSOL Axisymmetric Transient Heat Transfer

steps.title: Assign the Material
steps.explain: Assign the heat-only Material to the cylinder section.

steps.title: Resolve radius and height
steps.explain: Use a 12 × 16 quadratic lattice. Radius and axial length each have 25 mm elements. Time and spatial refinement are separate checks; the closing reference is not a license to skip them.

steps.title: Heat the curved wall
steps.explain: Prescribe the outer cylindrical wall at 1000 °C. The axis receives no condition: zero radial heat flow there follows from axisymmetry.

steps.title: Heat the first end
steps.explain: The bottom circular end is also held at 1000 °C. This is a finite cylinder: omitting end heating changes the benchmark.

steps.title: Heat the second end
steps.explain: The top end has the same prescribed temperature. The probe is 0.1 m from this end and 0.1 m from the axis, not at the cylinder centre.

steps.title: Start from cold, keep the history
steps.explain: Backward Euler with Δt = 2 s runs to 190 s from 0 °C. outputEvery = 19 retains a frame every 38 s and the final frame. This guide covers the maintained-temperature scenario only, not COMSOL’s later switch to insulation.

steps.title: Solve the warm-up
steps.explain: Run the transient Step. Probe temperature at [0.1 m, 0.3 m, 0 m] in the final frame. This mesh and Δt = 2 s give about 186.23 °C, against the published 190 s target 186.5 °C; inspect the recorded time before comparing, since a different frame answers a different question.

steps.title: Fit the section
steps.explain: Fit changes only the camera. Inspect the warm ends and rim and the cooler interior, then press Next.

steps.title: Check an independent answer
steps.explain: A benchmark is tied to its geometry, heating faces, time and probe coordinates. Replacing the axisymmetric idealisation with plane strain solves a different heat equation.
steps.theory:
For constant properties, $\alpha=k/(\rho c_p)=1.4400\times10^{-5}\,\mathrm{m^2/s}$. The separable cylindrical diffusion solution gives $T(r,z,t)=T_b[1-R(r,t)Z(z,t)]$, where $R$ is the zero-wall Bessel series and $Z$ the zero-end sine series. At $r=0.1\,\mathrm m$, $z=0.3\,\mathrm m$, $t=190\,\mathrm s$, it agrees with the published **186.5 °C** target. At Δt = 2, 1 and 0.5 s, backward Euler gives 186.2292, 186.3705 and 186.4417 °C. The automated check refines space and time independently and also catches a missing heated end.

**Try it:** use `query.probe` with `field: "temperature"`, `step: "warm-up"`, `at: ["0.1 m", "0.3 m", "0 m"]`; use the frame selector to inspect retained times. Rebuild and solve after changing the time step or mesh. A smaller time step reduces temporal error; it does not correct the wrong geometry or boundary conditions.

**Other solvers:** this is COMSOL’s 2D Axisymmetric / Time Dependent heat-transfer workflow, Abaqus axisymmetric heat-transfer elements with a transient heat-transfer Step, Ansys transient thermal axisymmetry, or Nastran transient heat transfer with axisymmetric elements. Names differ; the radial weighting and thermal initial/boundary conditions must agree.

Source: [COMSOL, Axisymmetric Transient Heat Transfer](https://doc.comsol.com/6.3/doc/com.comsol.help.models.mph.heat_transient_axi/heat_transient_axi.html), citing Cameron, Casey and Simpson, NAFEMS thermal benchmarks (1986).
